exposure: maternal drugs and alcohol consumption during pregnancy
mode of birth (cesarean vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 162 moderate-risk neonates (MRNs) aged 2-24 months who had been hospitalized in a NICU for at least 72 hours after birth, with a gestational age >= 34 weeks and birth weight >= 1500 g, and normal neurological and clinical examinations at hospital discharge.
finding: Thirty-four percent of moderate-risk neonates (MRNs) aged 2-24 months failed the neurodevelopmental screening test, with gross motor skills being the most affected area, and this rate widely exceeded that of the general population.
mod_finding: Infants born by cesarean delivery had a higher risk (OR: 2.2) of neurodevelopmental screening failure compared to those born by vaginal delivery.
